messages:
erin cho: FYI we saw a weird tail-latency + 429 pattern in the onboarding sampleapp this morning — embeds traffic started getting throttled even though embed QPS is low

rahul mehta: weird, are embeds and generate hitting the same quota? server-side quotas are per-key+route AFAIK

erin cho: logs show embed prefetchers were idle but new interactive generations were being throttled and vice-versa. dashboard shows client-side inflight pegged at limit even when only one endpoint was busy

minh tran: paste a small log snippet? curious whether the SDK is using a single global semaphore for all routes

erin cho: sanitized logs:
```
[2026-09-02T09:10:01Z] client:init windows: global=40 embeds=undefined gen=undefined
[2026-09-02T09:10:02Z] prefetch(embeds): start cursor=e1 inflight=18 global_inflight=18
[2026-09-02T09:10:03Z] user-gen: start req=r42 inflight=6 global_inflight=24
[2026-09-02T09:10:03Z] user-gen: status=429 reason=client_window limit=24 global_inflight=24
[2026-09-02T09:10:03Z] prefetch(embeds): status=200 cursor=e1 inflight=17 global_inflight=23
```

minh tran: aha. the JS SDK initializes only a global window unless you explicitly opt into per-endpoint windows. the Go SDK we borrowed the idea from had per-route weighted semaphores (embeds weight=1, gen weight=4) but JS defaulted to single window for simplicity

rahul mehta: so priority inversion: low-cost high-volume prefetches (embeds) hog slots and block interactive gens which need higher weight/priority. that explains the UX complaints where interactive latency climbs while background warmers stay busy

erin cho: exact repro: run two workers that continuously prefetch embeddings (window=20) and simultaneously fire occasional generate calls. gens get 429s despite overall server QPS being under the plan. simple repro script in Node attached in the PR

minh tran: suggested fixes:
1) change JS SDK default to per-endpoint windows mirroring Go (backwards compatible opt-out via `global_window=true`)
2) add slot weights and a priority queue so gen requests can preempt lower-priority background work when under pressure
3) expose per-client config `endpoint_windows: { embeds: 16, generate: 8 }` in sampleapp config and docs

rahul mehta: short-term mitigation for onboarding: reduce embed prefetch window to 6 and set `generate_priority=true` in sampleapp. also add a note to onboarding doc: "If interactive calls seem throttled while background prefetchers run, lower prefetch window or enable per-endpoint windows."

ci-bot: canary deploy requested: sampleapp-staging config update by @erin cho

erin cho: opened issue to audit SDK parity across languages — Go supports weighted per-route windows, Python has a hybrid, JS was global-only. we should align defaults to reduce surprising UX across SDKs

minh tran: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789 adds `endpoint_windows` opt-in, docs, and a small priority queue. follow-up: add regression test in the sampleapp stress harness that mixes high-rate low-cost embeds + low-rate high-cost gens

rahul mehta: added a short blurb to onboarding cheatsheet and the quickstart example to show `endpoint_windows` usage

erin cho: monitoring after canary looks much better; interactive latency dropped and 429s stopped in the next 10m. leaving the thread here in case folks want to follow parity audit

minh tran: filing internal ticket to standardize the schema for endpoint weighting across SDKs so we can enforce parity in CI

erin cho: thanks all :thumbsup:
